record.original_question: Let ℘(n) be the parameter space of Euclidean n-gons up to scaling, equipped on each combinatorial component with the corresponding Lebesgue measure and normalized to a probability measure λ. Let 𝓔(n)⊂℘(n) be the set of ergodic n-gons. Is λ(𝓔(n)) positive?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n\geq 3$, let $\mathscr{P}(n)$ denote the parameter space of Euclidean $n$-gons considered up to similarity (i.e., up to scaling, rotation, and translation). The space $\mathscr{P}(n)$ decomposes into finitely many combinatorial components, each of which carries a natural finite-dimensional Lebesgue measure inherited from a parametrization (e.g., by side lengths and angles, modulo the closing conditions). Normalize these component-wise Lebesgue measures so that their disjoint union gives a probability measure $\lambda$ on $\mathscr{P}(n)$.

Call an $n$-gon $P$ ergodic if the billiard flow on $P$ (the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle, with elastic reflection at the boundary) is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure. Let $\mathcal{E}(n)\subset\mathscr{P}(n)$ denote the set of ergodic $n$-gons.

It is known that $\mathcal{E}(n)$ is residual in $\mathscr{P}(n)$ in the sense of Baire category. Determine whether
$$\lambda(\mathcal{E}(n)) > 0.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Multiple recent surveys on billiard dynamics list this as an open problem: while the set of ergodic polygons is known to be residual (Baire-generic) in the parameter space, it is not known whether it has positive Lebesgue measure. Numerical experiments suggest typical triangles are ergodic, but no proof is known even for $n=3$.

status_evidence.claim: Listed explicitly as an open problem in a recent billiard dynamics survey.

status_evidence.title: On the ergodicity of billiards in non-rational polygons
status_evidence.snippet: It is unclear whether the set of ergodic billiards has positive Lebesgue measure.
status_evidence.claim: Ergodicity of typical polygonal billiards remains unresolved.
